We introduce a novel deep architecture for wide baseline stereo that learns to find good correspondes, and is able to improve the state of art with little training.

(1) a deep network can be used to learn to label sparse correspondences as inlier or outliers and to estimate the relative pose of two cameras, and that (2) the network should be trained in an end-to- end fashion to jointly learn these tasks.

(1) we introduce a deep learning architecture for learning correspondences, (2) we introduce a novel normalization method, called Context Normalizaiton, that allows the use of deep learning architectures on sparse data, (3) we demonstrate that our method can improve the state of art in wide-baseline stereo on multiple challenging datasets with very little training data, and (4) our method can be applied to any other correspondence problem.
